discovery_target: Previously unreported autonomous sender-to-recipient coordination in which task work is transferred, used by a distinguishable recipient, and the cooperation crosses an operator-defined boundary
selection: Completed the exact final sixteen-record nghttp2.org cursor saved by Pass 63, then rotated into all twelve untouched exact-ID comparison overlaps carrying the listing-level sink-domain cue. Original JSON was assessed for exact-source chronology, source-level transfer/use operations, sanitized channel chronology, archived request and response sizes, domain-level traffic and public state/report references. The three saved committed-record locator queries were then run, excluding this repository before inference.
snapshot_limitations: The sanitized snapshots preserve public report links, separate event and observation times, report and decoded-source hashes, bounded static structure, channel-reference hashes and domain-level recorded traffic. They omit carrier paths, channel names, request and response bodies, headers, submitter and network-origin values, visualization URLs, credentials, personal addresses and recovered source. Static counts and endpoint hashes are review cues, not participant identity, task meaning, causal use or authorization evidence.

strongest_apparent_dependencies.assessment: Four decoded sources each repeat exactly twice, with gaps of one to three seconds. This tight repetition supports duplicate submission or scanner retry; none of the pairs preserves a foreign result, reply or later causal use.

One submitted page records six GETs to one sanitized notification-channel hash. All six request bodies and archived responses are empty, no write to the hash appears in this cohort and the source contains no response-read operation or task term. This is empty polling, not a transfer/use edge.

Two sources assign navigation to an example domain and fourteen carry the older peer-language cue. The network requests return 404 and the source language resolves to Tableau browser/UI terminology; the strict task-or-peer count is zero and no autonomous recipient is visible.

nghttp2_closure_assessment.assessment: The final nghttp2 slice closes the saved host cursor inside the known AIHW Tableau browser-test family. Source duplication, empty channel reads, metadata navigation and visualization traffic do not establish distinguishable autonomous participants, transferred task work, recipient use or an operator-boundary crossing.
nghttp2_closure_assessment.classification: Known AIHW comparison-overlap browser-test sequence; no autonomous transfer/use edge

webhook_get_controls.prior_snapshot_overlap: Both sanitized channel hashes already occur in earlier known-AIHW shortener or sink review snapshots.
webhook_get_controls.assessment: The repeated channel references are GET-only, empty and partly rate-limited. They preserve neither a producer artifact nor recipient acquisition and use.

singleton_post_control.assessment: One submitted program posts twice and reads the service response. The archive metadata records zero request-body characters, no second independently attributable consumer and no later work that depends on the response. This same-page publish response is consistent with a service acknowledgement, not a sender-to-recipient task exchange.

sink_domain_overlap_assessment.assessment: The twelve sink-domain records are another exact-ID segment of the known AIHW comparison family. Empty GET polling, a singleton same-page publish/acknowledgement and shared visualization traffic fail the required participant, task-transfer, downstream-use and authorization tests.
sink_domain_overlap_assessment.classification: Known AIHW comparison-overlap channel controls; no autonomous transfer/use edge
